items.title: Piles of heavy snow will again be cleared from all driveways in Mississauga
items.summary: City snowplow crews are preparing to once again clear heavy snowy messes — or windrows — from the driveways of all Mississauga homes as winter approaches. The City of Mississauga’s winter maintenance teams for the first time ever last year cleared all residential driveways of the difficult-to-move piles of hard-packed snow and sometimes ice as part of regular seasonal maintenance services. Windrows, left behind at the end of driveways after the streets have been plowed, were a contentious issue in Mississauga for several years before residents finally pushed city council hard enough to deliver a winter plan to keep their driveways accessible. Helen Noehammer, director of works operations and maintenance for the City of Mississauga, told INSAUGA Canada this week the windrow-clearing service “was well received overall” by residents last winter. ” As the cold, snowy weather approaches in the coming weeks and months, Noehammer reminds Mississauga residents to do their part to ensure windrow clearing goes as smoothly as possible. To allow snowplows easy access to driveways, residents must remove parked vehicles from the street when a citywide winter parking restriction is declared during periods of heavy snowfall, Noehammer said. Parked vehicles left on the road, including those in 15-hour parking areas (new this year), may be subject to a fine of $150 or towing, she added.

items.title: Mississauga accepting cycling recognition awards nominations until Jan. 8
items.summary: Awards will be handed out in spring during a council meeting. The Mississauga Cycling Advisory Committee hosts a past bike ride. Nominations for its 2026 cycling advocacy awards are open until Jan. 8, 2027. Mississauga’s Cycling Advisory Committee is calling for nominations to recognize individuals, local businesses, and students who have promoted cycling and active transportation across the city throughout 2026. For the annual recognition, four categories are open: To qualify, nominees must be residents of Mississauga and must not have won an advisory committee award in the past four years. Current committee members, city employees, Peel Region employees working in cycling or sustainable transportation and their immediate family members are ineligible. To nominate someone, a form must be submitted with details of the nominee’s contribution and two supporting letters from individuals or organizations. Self-nominations are also accepted. ca by Jan. m. The advisory committee will review nominations and recipients will be awarded in spring 2027 at a council meeting.

items.title: Peel Public Health Hands Out Six Conditional Passes After Mississauga Restaurant Inspections
items.summary: According to Peel Public Health, six Mississauga restaurants received a conditional pass rather than the usual green sign during recent food safety inspections. The health unit said inspectors regularly check restaurants, cocktail bars, beverage rooms, bakeries and takeout establishments across the region to confirm compliance with the Health Protection and Promotion Act. Peel Public Health explained a green pass tells customers a business is meeting food safety and operational requirements, while a conditional pass signals an issue inspectors found. The health unit reports Aghati Restaurant, at 2575 Dundas St. in Mississauga, was inspected Oct. 27 and received a conditional pass. According to Peel Public Health, a second Mississauga location was inspected Oct. 22 as part of the same round of checks. The health unit's inspection program continues on a rolling basis throughout the year.

items.title: New Mayor's Affordability Push Freezes Mississauga's Big Arts-Centre Overhaul
items.summary: According to insauga.com, plans to tear down Mississauga's Living Arts Centre and replace it with a larger performing arts venue have stalled following Monday's mayoral election. The outlet reports mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo spoke to media at Celebration Square, steps from the LAC, the morning after his win and reiterated the affordability message from his campaign. Insauga.com says Tedjo argued that building an entirely new, costly downtown core featuring a convention centre, hotel and performing arts facility should not be a top priority during difficult financial times. The outlet reports the proposal originated earlier this year under outgoing mayor Carolyn Parrish and city council. According to insauga.com, Tedjo defeated Parrish by 22,626 votes and former mayor Bonnie Crombie by 31,288 votes, while Ward 7 Coun. Dipika Damerla finished fourth with 11,500 votes. The outlet notes it remains unclear whether the downtown plan will move forward now that a new mayor has taken office.

items.title: Culham Trail Access Point Reopens as Eglinton Avenue Sewer Upgrade Wraps Up
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Peel Region has finished upgrading the sanitary sewer and maintenance holes along a stretch of Eglinton Avenue West near Mississauga Road. According to the outlet, region officials said all construction work between Hewicks Lane and The Chase is now complete. The outlet reports the project upgraded sewers that carry wastewater from sinks, tubs, showers and toilets, a task officials said was needed to keep providing high-quality wastewater service. According to insauga.com, traffic on Eglinton Avenue West is expected to return to normal now that the work is done. The outlet reports the completed project also means the Eglinton Avenue West and Barbertown Road access point to the Culham Trail, closed to the public since earlier this year, will reopen.

items.title: Tedjo beat 2 incumbents in Mississauga's mayoral race. Here are his plans for the city
items.summary: One day after a decisive victory, Alvin Tedjo announced his priorities as the next mayor of Mississauga, saying he will focus on affordability, crime, housing, transportation and the economy.

items.title: Mississauga's Incoming Council Takes Office Nov. 16 With Nine Incumbents, Two New Faces
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports nine incumbent city councillors kept their seats in Monday's election, while two new members will join the council table. According to the outlet, the new council will be sworn in at an inaugural ceremony on Nov. 16, with its first general committee meeting set for Nov. 18. The outlet reports mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo, a one-term Ward 2 councillor, won a sweeping victory with 74,479 votes. According to mississauga.com, incumbent Carolyn Parrish received 51,853 votes, former mayor Bonnie Crombie received 43,191 votes and Ward 7's Dipika Damerla received 11,500 votes. The outlet reports Tedjo addressed supporters with his family beside him at his election-night party at Wildflower Event Space.

items.title: Tedjo Sets 100-Day Clock on Affordability as He Takes Selfies With Supporters at Celebration Square
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports Mississauga mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo took selfies with supporters in Celebration Square the morning after his underdog victory, promising to tackle affordability within his first 100 days in office. According to the newspaper, Tedjo told reporters at his first press conference as incoming mayor that he was encouraged by voter turnout of 34 per cent, up from 22 per cent in 2022. The Star reports Tedjo acknowledged the political battle with Carolyn Parrish and Bonnie Crombie will continue inside council chambers as he tries to deliver on campaign promises. According to the outlet, those promises include freezing property taxes and setting up a new Mississauga housing corporation modeled on Toronto's CreateTO. The Star reports Tedjo also pledged to address concerns from businesses in Ridgeway Plaza and the surrounding community.

items.title: Four High-Profile Candidates Pushed Mississauga Turnout Past 2022 Levels, Insauga Reports
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Mississauga's bitterly contested mayoral race drew considerably more eligible voters to the polls than the city saw in the 2022 municipal election. According to the outlet, the matchup between incumbent Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie was widened further by one-term councillor and now mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo, who had already challenged Parrish once before in the 2024 byelection to succeed Crombie. The outlet reports Ward 7 councillor Dipika Damerla, who finished a distant fourth and is leaving council as a result, rounded out the four high-profile names that helped drive turnout. According to insauga.com, 191,166 voters cast ballots this time to elect the mayor, 11 city councillors and a slate of school board trustees. The outlet notes that despite the stronger showing, Mississauga's turnout has historically ranked among the lowest in Ontario.

items.title: Peel Police Suspend Toronto Man's Licence After Street Race Near Meadowvale Boulevard
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Peel Regional Police have laid multiple charges against a Toronto man after a street-racing investigation in northwest Mississauga. According to the outlet, officers with the force's Safer Roads Team spotted a vehicle racing with other cars near Meadowpine Boulevard and Meadowvale Boulevard in the early morning hours of Oct. 15. Police said the vehicle was travelling at a high speed in close proximity to pedestrians, creating a significant risk to public safety. The outlet reports investigators identified a suspect and arrested 21-year-old Anthony Fuellos Knox of Toronto that same day. According to insauga.com, Knox was released on an undertaking to appear in Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton, while Safer Roads Team officers seized his vehicle and suspended his driver's licence for 30 days.

items.title: High School Teacher Says He Saw Mayor-elect Coming When Tedjo Was Still a Student
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports Alvin Tedjo's former high school teacher said he always expected his student would one day become mayor. According to the newspaper, Tony Oseivhi, who taught communications technology, made the comment after attending Tedjo's first press conference as mayor-elect, held in Celebration Square just minutes from Father Michael Goetz Secondary School. The Star reports Oseivhi joked that Tedjo was already a politician back in high school. According to the outlet, Oseivhi said his former student has always been a skilled communicator. The Star reports Oseivhi said he was "so excited" about his former student's victory.
